attributes.name: Druva - Administrator Impossible Travel
attributes.description: Detects the same Druva administrator successfully authenticating from two or more countries within 60 minutes, which may indicate impossible travel or compromised credentials.
author: Druva
false_positives: An administrator legitimately using geographically separated VPN or secure-access egress points.
Corporate proxy, cloud security service, or mobile carrier routing that causes large apparent geographic changes.
GeoIP inaccuracies or reassignment of IP address geolocation.
Approved travel combined with remote-access infrastructure that makes the calculated travel speed unreliable.
tags: Druva Detection Pack 0 – Core Cyber Resilience
attributes.query:
FROM logs-druva.event-*
| WHERE druva.feature == "Admin Event"
    AND druva.event_type == "Admin Login"
    AND event.outcome == "success"
    AND user.email IS NOT NULL
    AND source.ip IS NOT NULL
    AND source.geo.location IS NOT NULL

| STATS
    login_count = COUNT_DISTINCT(event.id),
    ip_count = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip),
    first_login = MIN(@timestamp),
    last_login = MAX(@timestamp),
    first_location = FIRST(source.geo.location, @timestamp),
    last_location = LAST(source.geo.location, @timestamp),
    first_ip = FIRST(source.ip, @timestamp),
    last_ip = LAST(source.ip, @timestamp)
  BY user.email

| WHERE login_count >= 2
    AND ip_count >= 2
    AND last_login > first_login

| EVAL
    elapsed_minutes = DATE_DIFF("minutes", first_login, last_login),
    distance_meters = ST_DISTANCE(first_location, last_location)

| WHERE elapsed_minutes > 0
    AND elapsed_minutes <= 60
    AND distance_meters >= 500000

| EVAL implied_speed_kmh =
    (distance_meters / 1000.0) / (elapsed_minutes / 60.0)

| WHERE implied_speed_kmh >= 900
attributes.note:
### Investigation guide

This rule detects successful Druva administrator authentication from geographically distant source locations within 60 minutes where the implied travel speed is at least 900 km/h. This may indicate use of compromised cloud-account credentials.

#### Investigation steps

- Identify the administrator, source IP addresses, timestamps, and geographic locations contributing to the alert.
- Validate GeoIP accuracy and determine whether either address belongs to a VPN, proxy, corporate gateway, mobile provider, or security service.
- Confirm whether the administrator was traveling or intentionally using multiple network egress locations.
- Review successful and failed administrator logins before and after the alert.
- Review role changes, API credential activity, downloads, protection changes, repository changes, and other sensitive actions performed by the account.
- Determine whether authentication or session information indicates unauthorized access.

#### Response

- Contact the administrator through a trusted channel when compromise is suspected.
- Revoke or rotate affected credentials and sessions according to organizational procedure.
- Review all privileged actions performed during the suspicious access window.
